text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000112 bills 99215 well above expectation across every complexity band, but the small set of returned charts supports the billed level, so the pattern cannot yet be attributed to upcoding or to panel acuity.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 excess is concentrated in sicker patients, since most 99215s fall on patients with 4 or more conditions, which fits a complex panel. However, this provider's 99215 share is roughly double the all-provider share in every complexity band, including 0–2 conditions, so higher acuity alone does not explain it. The records review leans toward legitimacy, with none of the 13 documented 99215s falling below the billed level, but that sample is small and covers only about 4% of claims. Some documentation warrants a closer look: C0062089 is a 22-year-old with no chronic conditions and a back-pain diagnosis whose note records high MDM with no time, which could reflect inflated or templated notes. The few moderate-or-higher data-reviewed notes without a lab line are only weak evidence. A reviewer should first pull charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s (e.g., C0062089, C0063125, C0063236, C0062726) and a larger random set of 99215s, checking whether the MDM narrative is patient-specific or cloned across visits."}
